html:
The Guyana and Venezuela territorial dispute is Venezuela's claim to the land west of the Essequibo River, about two-thirds of Guyana. A tribunal in Paris gave most of it to British Guiana in 1899.

Venezuela accepted the award for decades, but in 1962 declared it void, saying the judges had made a deal behind its back. The Geneva Agreement of 1966, signed just before independence, set up talks that never settled the matter. In 2018 Guyana took the case to the International Court of Justice.

After the oil finds off the coast, Venezuela held a referendum in December 2023 backing a new Venezuelan state in the region. The two presidents agreed soon after not to use force. The dispute goes back to the borders of the Dutch colonies.
sum: The Guyana and Venezuela territorial dispute is Venezuela's claim to the land west of the Essequibo River, about two-thirds of Guyana. A tribunal in Paris gave most of it to British Guiana in 1899.
